title: AI contribution policy
description: Rules large projects set for AI-assisted work. Enable the ones your project or target repository requires.

rules.title: A human owns the change
rules.text: A human must review, understand and be able to explain every change before it is submitted.

rules.title: No autonomous posting
rules.text: Do not open issues or pull requests, or post comments, on a person's behalf without their review.

rules.title: Approval before push
rules.text: Show a summary of the changes and wait for explicit approval before running git push. "Open a PR" is intent, not permission.

rules.title: No PR unless asked
rules.text: Do not create a pull request unless the user explicitly asks for one.

rules.title: Disclose AI assistance
rules.text: Disclose meaningful AI assistance in the PR description, in the form the project template asks for.

rules.title: Follow the trailer rules
rules.text: Follow the project trailer convention for AI assistance. Some projects require Assisted-by and forbid Co-authored-by for an agent.

rules.title: Humans sign off
rules.text: Leave Signed-off-by to the human author. An agent never signs off a commit.

rules.title: No promotion
rules.text: Do not use commit messages or PR text to promote products or brands.

rules.title: Stop at a policy gate
rules.text: When a project policy bans a kind of work, stop and explain the policy instead of offering the same output under another name.

rules.title: Guide, do not just solve
rules.text: If the user cannot yet explain the change, point to the relevant code and let them shape the approach before you write it.

rules.title: Personal-use exemption
rules.text: Some limits relax for work that will never be shared. Apply that exemption only when the user states it explicitly.

rules.title: Human-written PR text
rules.text: Where a project requires human-written PR descriptions, commit messages and review replies, do not draft them.
